questions.question: A proton ($m = 1.67\times10^{-27}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $q = 1.6\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$) moves at $v = 2\times10^6\ \mathrm{m/s}$ perpendicular to a magnetic field $B = 0.4\ \mathrm{T}$. Find: (a) the radius of the circular orbit, (b) the period of revolution.
Derive the radius $r = mv/(qB)$ for a charged particle moving in a circle in a uniform magnetic field. Then show the period $T = 2\pi m/(qB)$ is independent of speed.
questions.answer:
The magnetic force provides the centripetal acceleration:

$qvB = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$

$r = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$ ✓

**Period:** circumference = $2\pi r$, speed = $v$:

$T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{v} = \dfrac{2\pi}{v} \cdot \dfrac{mv}{qB} = \dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ ✓

The period depends only on $m$, $q$, $B$ — **not on velocity** $v$. This is the **isochronous** property of cyclotron motion, exploited in cyclotron accelerators.

questions.question: An alpha particle ($m = 6.64\times10^{-27}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $q = 3.2\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$) moves in a circle of radius $r = 10\ \mathrm{cm}$ in a field $B = 0.5\ \mathrm{T}$. Find: (a) the speed, (b) the kinetic energy in eV.
Compare the radii of a proton and an electron moving at the same speed $v$ in the same magnetic field $B$. ($m_p = 1.67\times10^{-27}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $m_e = 9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$)
questions.answer:
Both have the same $|q| = e$, so $r = mv/(eB) \propto m$:

$\dfrac{r_p}{r_e} = \dfrac{m_p}{m_e} = \dfrac{1.67\times10^{-27}}{9.11\times10^{-31}} \approx 1836$

A proton orbits in a circle about **1836 times larger** than an electron at the same speed.

The electron's orbit is much tighter — this is why in a cloud chamber, heavy particles leave straighter tracks than electrons.

questions.question: A mass spectrometer uses a magnetic field $B = 0.3\ \mathrm{T}$ to deflect ions. A singly ionized atom ($q = e$) is accelerated from rest through $V = 1500\ \mathrm{V}$ before entering the field. Find the radius of the circular path.
questions.answer:
Ion kinetic energy from acceleration:

$KE = qV = eV$

$\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = eV \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2eV}{m}}$

Radius: $r = \dfrac{mv}{eB} = \dfrac{m}{eB}\sqrt{\dfrac{2eV}{m}} = \dfrac{1}{B}\sqrt{\dfrac{2mV}{e}}$

For carbon-12 ($m = 12 \times 1.67\times10^{-27} = 2.004\times10^{-26}\ \mathrm{kg}$):

$r = \dfrac{1}{0.3}\sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 2.004\times10^{-26} \times 1500}{1.6\times10^{-19}}}$

$= \dfrac{1}{0.3}\sqrt{\dfrac{6.012\times10^{-23}}{1.6\times10^{-19}}} = \dfrac{1}{0.3}\sqrt{3.757\times10^{-4}} = \dfrac{0.01938}{0.3} \approx 0.065\ \mathrm{m}$

questions.question: A cyclotron accelerates protons with $B = 1.5\ \mathrm{T}$. Find: (a) the cyclotron frequency (frequency at which the accelerating voltage must alternate), (b) the speed and radius when the proton exits with kinetic energy $KE = 10\ \mathrm{MeV}$.

An electron ($m = 9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$) travels in a circle of radius $r = 5\ \mathrm{cm}$ in a field $B = 2\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{T}$. Find: (a) the speed, (b) the frequency of revolution.

Two particles with the same charge $q$ but different masses $m_1 = m$ and $m_2 = 2m$ are accelerated from rest through the same potential $V$ and then enter the same magnetic field $B$ perpendicularly. Find the ratio of their circular radii $r_2/r_1$.
questions.answer:
After acceleration: $\frac{1}{2}m_i v_i^2 = qV \Rightarrow v_i = \sqrt{2qV/m_i}$

Radius: $r_i = \dfrac{m_i v_i}{qB} = \dfrac{m_i}{qB}\sqrt{\dfrac{2qV}{m_i}} = \dfrac{1}{qB}\sqrt{2qVm_i} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2qVm_i}}{qB}$

$\dfrac{r_2}{r_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{m_2}{m_1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{m}} = \sqrt{2}$

The heavier particle has a radius $\sqrt{2}$ times larger — this is the basis of mass spectrometry.

questions.question: A charged particle enters a magnetic field at an angle $\alpha$ to the field direction. Describe its trajectory and find the pitch (distance traveled along the field per revolution).
questions.answer:
Decompose velocity: $v_\| = v\cos\alpha$ (parallel to $B$, no force), $v_\perp = v\sin\alpha$ (perpendicular to $B$).

**Trajectory:** The perpendicular component gives circular motion with radius $r = mv_\perp/(qB) = mv\sin\alpha/(qB)$. The parallel component gives uniform translation along $B$. Combined: **helical motion**.

**Pitch** (distance along $B$ per revolution):

$p = v_\| \times T = v\cos\alpha \times \dfrac{2\pi m}{qB} = \dfrac{2\pi mv\cos\alpha}{qB}$

Special cases: $\alpha = 0$: no circular motion, straight line. $\alpha = 90°$: circle, zero pitch.

questions.question: A particle of charge $q$ and mass $m$ moves in a circle of radius $r$ in field $B$. Show that its kinetic energy can be written as $KE = \dfrac{q^2B^2r^2}{2m}$.
questions.answer:
From the radius formula: $r = mv/(qB) \Rightarrow v = qBr/m$

Kinetic energy:

$KE = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}m\left(\dfrac{qBr}{m}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}m \cdot \dfrac{q^2B^2r^2}{m^2}$

$$KE = \dfrac{q^2B^2r^2}{2m}$$ ✓

This is useful in mass spectrometry: by measuring $r$, you can determine $m$ (knowing $q$ and $B$), or determine $KE$ directly from $r$.
